payload.text:
I'd hold the merge. The extension parsing doesn't do what the README says, so almost every real filename gets the wrong content type. I didn't edit anything; I only read the diff and ran the tests and some sample filenames on a clean checkout. The tests pass, but they don't catch this.

**Blocker: `src/extension.js`**
`name.split('.')[1]` takes the text after the *first* dot and never lowercases it. The README says it should be the text after the *last* dot, lowercased. Here's what it actually returns:

| Input | Returns | README expects | Content type it gets |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Archive.TAR.GZ` | `TAR` | `gz` | octet-stream (should be gzip) |
| `photo.JPG` | `JPG` | `jpg` | octet-stream (should be jpeg) |
| `a.b.c.png` | `b` | `png` | octet-stream (should be png) |
| `README` | `undefined` | `''` | octet-stream |
| `file.` | `''` | `''` | ✓ |

Only lowercase names with a single dot work, and that's the only case the test checks. A fix would find the last dot, return `''` if there's no dot or it's the last character, and otherwise lowercase what follows it. Then add tests for each row above.

**Smaller issues**
- **`safeName`:** it does stop path traversal, because every `/` and `\` becomes `_` (`a/../../etc/passwd` → `a_.._.._etc_passwd`). But `..` or `...` becomes an empty string, so the caller would store a file with no name. It should fall back to a default name or reject the upload. Also, `.htaccess` becomes `htaccess`. That's probably intended, but worth knowing.
- **Content-type tests:** `contentType` has no tests of its own. A few would have caught the blocker.
- **Type list:** `TYPES` has no entry for `jpeg`, so `photo.jpeg` will be served as octet-stream. That may be a deliberate choice.

The version bump, CHANGELOG and README changes are fine. The README's description of safe names matches what the code does.
